questions.question: Explain how Mapungubwe was linked to the wider world before Europeans arrived.
questions.expected_answer: Mapungubwe was part of the Indian Ocean trade. Porters carried gold and ivory on foot to Sofala and other East African coastal towns, and Swahili, Arab, Persian and Indian traders sailed dhows with the monsoon winds to Arabia, India and China, bringing back glass beads, cloth and porcelain.

questions.question: Why did Europeans in the 1400s want to find a sea route to the East?
questions.expected_answer: Europeans wanted spices, silk and precious stones from India, China and South-East Asia. These goods came along long land and sea routes through the Middle East, passing through many middlemen who each added to the price, so they were very expensive. A sea route around Africa would let Europeans buy them directly and more cheaply.

questions.question: Why do historians say that southern Africa was not really found by Europeans?
questions.expected_answer: Southern Africa was not empty or lost. The Khoikhoi, the San and African farming communities had lived there for a very long time, and the region was already linked to the world by the Indian Ocean trade. It was only new to the Europeans, so historians try to tell the story from more than one point of view.
